answers.docs.gaps:
Nothing I found was *wrong*. Four gaps:

**Whether `Output::Binary` survives the structured modes.**
docs/crates/dispatch/topics/handler-contract.md says only "Binary output
bypasses the render function entirely", and docs/topics/output-modes.md says
of the structured modes that they "bypass the template entirely. Handler data
is serialized directly". Neither says which wins for a binary result. The
whole plumbing contract in this spec rests on the answer, so I tested it:
`gitlike ref-list --output json|yaml|xml|csv|term|text|term-debug|auto` all
produce the identical 41 bytes. That is the behavior I wanted, but I had to
discover it rather than read it.

**`RunError::kind()` and `ExitStatus`.** See question 4. The prose names the
variants (`ClapUsage`, `Handler`, `Hook(phase)`, `Render`,
`FinalWrite(...)`, `External`) but no signature; docs/ has no accessor for
turning an `ExitStatus` into a number, which every application that owns its
own final write needs.

**Empty CSS rules.** docs/crates/render/topics/styling-system.md documents the
supported attributes but never says whether `.hash { }` registers a style name
with no attributes or is skipped as junk. It registers it — which is what
makes an unstyled theme expressible in CSS — but I confirmed that by running,
not by reading.

**`ExternalFailure` for an application's own status.**
docs/topics/error-handling.md scopes it narrowly: "Use `ExternalFailure` only
when another operation owns the status and diagnostic contract, such as a
delegated Git invocation… this is not a general exit-code mapping mechanism."
It is also the only documented way for a handler to choose any nonzero status
other than 1, and this spec pins statuses 1 and 3 to application conditions
with no external process involved. I used it, against the letter of that
sentence, because the alternative is `process::exit` in a handler, which the
same page forbids. A documented seam for an application-owned exit status
would close this.

**Not a gap, but worth recording:** I could not exercise the pager end-to-end.
The sandbox has no pseudo-terminal (`script: openpty: Operation not
permitted`, and Python's `pty.openpty()` fails with "out of pty devices"), so
the `stdout().is_terminal()` branch never became true in a real run. The
decision table and the pager write itself are unit-tested directly, and the
"never paged when piped" half is covered end-to-end.
answers.friction:
**Getting an exit status out of a captured run.** docs/topics/execution-outcomes.md
shows `assert_eq!(result.exit_status(), Some(ExitStatus::SUCCESS));` and says
of `External` that "its `exit_status()` is the exact declared nonzero status",
but never says how to turn an `ExitStatus` into a process exit code, and the
`Some(...)` in the example made `RunError::kind()` look optional too. I
resolved both by compiling a probe and reading:

```
174 |         DispatchResult::Error(error) => match error.kind() {
    |                                               ------------ this expression has type `RunErrorKind`
176 |             Some(RunErrorKind::External) => {
    |             ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ expected `RunErrorKind`, found `Option<_>`
```

```
229 | fn probe(e: &standout::cli::RunError) -> i32 { e.exit_status().code() }
    |                                                ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ expected `i32`, found `u8`
```

**Nothing pages command output.** docs/topics/standout-help.md: "The one thing
the two paths cannot share is `--page`, because paging is a terminal side
effect and only a *printing* entry point may perform it." Paging exists for
`help --page` and nowhere else, so a spec that pages `log` has to take the
final write back with `run_with`. That is a coherent boundary, but it means
the spec's "porcelain pages, plumbing never does" cannot be expressed as
configuration; it is application code in `main`.

**The trailing-newline contract shaped the template.** From
docs/crates/render/topics/templating.md: "The engine consumes exactly one
final newline… The process edge appends exactly one." A per-line `{% for %}`
loop therefore renders one newline too many, because the loop body's newline
is not the template's final one. `log.jinja` emits the separator ahead of each
line but the first (`{% if not loop.first %}`) to land on exactly three lines.

**The unstyled theme could not simply omit its styles.**
docs/crates/render/topics/styling-system.md: "`Term` | Unknown tags get a `?`
marker: `[unknown?]text[/unknown?]`". So a `mono` theme that just leaves
`.hash`/`.message`/`.author`/`.branch` undefined would corrupt the output
under `--output term`. `mono.css` defines all four with empty rule bodies
instead.

answers.summary:
`gitlike` as specified in SPEC.md, complete and working. `cargo build` and
`cargo test` both succeed (19 unit tests + 17 end-to-end tests against the
compiled binary, all passing), and I verified every command by running the
binary.

Shape:

- `src/repo.rs` — the frozen repository, CLI-free.
- `src/config.rs` — config resolution, taking an explicit cwd and environment
  so the whole precedence chain (flag > nearest `.gitlike.toml` > user file >
  default) is testable without touching the process.
- `src/plumbing.rs` — the plumbing byte contract, built as bytes rather than
  as a template.
- `src/handlers.rs` — `#[handler]` adapters; `src/views.rs` — the view DTOs.
- `src/templates/{log,status}.jinja`, `src/styles/{default,mono}.css` —
  porcelain presentation.
- `src/pager.rs` + `main.rs` — the paging decision and the final write.

Two design decisions carry most of the spec:

- Porcelain (`log`, `status`) goes through the normal render pipeline, so it
  is themed, degrades to plain when piped, and gets `--output json|yaml|…`
  for free.
- Plumbing (`ref-list`, `cat-object`) and `config get` return
  `Output::Binary`, which bypasses rendering entirely. That is what makes
  their bytes identical under every theme, every `--output` mode, and
  terminal-vs-pipe — I verified all eight `--output` values plus both themes
  plus `NO_COLOR` produce the same bytes.
- `main` uses `run_with` and performs the final write itself, because paging
  is a terminal side effect that standout deliberately leaves to a printing
  entry point. Plumbing is written raw; porcelain goes through the pager when
  one applies.

Exit statuses: 0 success, 1 `config get` on an unset key, 2 clap usage errors,
3 unknown object hash. The two application-chosen statuses are declared with
`ExternalFailure`, which preserves the status and the verbatim stderr payload.
answers.workarounds:
**`--no-pager` is read off argv, not out of `ArgMatches`** (`src/main.rs`).
It is a properly declared global clap flag — clap parses and validates it, and
it shows up in help — but the paging decision happens in `main` after dispatch
has finished, where the parsed matches are gone. Re-parsing with
`Cli::try_parse_from` would fail on standout's own augmented flags
(`--output`, `--output-file-path`), so `gitlike log --no-pager --output json`
would silently lose the flag. The scan skips argv[0] and stops at `--`, so a
positional can never be mistaken for the flag; in any case no porcelain
command takes a positional, so the scan has no observable failure mode here.

**`ExternalFailure::new(1, String::new())`** in `handlers::config::get` — an
empty diagnostic is how `config get` on an unset key prints nothing on either
stream while exiting 1. See question 5 for why `ExternalFailure` at all.

**Empty CSS rule bodies in `src/styles/mono.css`** — `.hash { }` and friends
exist only to keep the tags "known" so `--output term` does not decorate them
with `?` markers.

**`NO_COLOR` selects the `mono` theme in addition to suppressing the
destination's color capability** (`src/main.rs`). Clearing
`TargetProperties::stdout_color_capability` covers `auto`, but
docs/topics/output-modes.md is explicit that "`NO_COLOR=1 myapp list
--output=term` still emits ANSI", and the spec says `NO_COLOR` disables
styling in porcelain output with no exception for a requested mode. Selecting
the unstyled theme is what covers the `--output term` case.

**Invalid configuration is ignored rather than rejected** (`src/config.rs`) —
unparseable TOML, a `log.limit` that is not a positive integer, an unreadable
file. SPEC.md's exit-code table has no status for a bad config file, so
contributing nothing is the reading that keeps the documented statuses exact.
A file that exists but parses to nothing still ends the upward walk, since the
spec says the first file found wins.
